result.reasoning:
The mechanism ops7 describes is real, but it is not a defect: it is this file's documented-by-behaviour convention for every arity-2 `day_*` op, the kernel's output is a valid and exactly-specified estimand (never an arithmetically wrong number), the production call sites are almost all unaffected, the claimed 24%-166% magnitude is a near-zero-denominator artifact of the reporter's harness, and the suggested code change would be a regression.

1) MECHANISM REPRODUCED, OUTPUT CORRECT. `day_topw_mean` (ops_ext.py:575-585) does compute the 0.9 quantile over `ok = isfinite(y) & isfinite(w)`, so the reported 10-minute case returns 2.0. But 2.0 is the right answer under the op's actual (joint-finite-pool) definition. Over 400 randomized trials (M=1..60, 30% independent NaN in each argument) the kernel: (a) never produced a value outside [min, max] of y over the joint-finite minutes (0/400), (b) was finite exactly when some minute had both arguments finite (0/400 mismatches), (c) matched an independently-written numpy implementation of "top decile by |w| of the joint-finite pool" to 1e-9 (0/400 mismatches). There is no arithmetic error to find; the two candidate readings are two different well-defined estimands.

2) IT IS THE FILE'S CONVENTION, AND THE REPORTER'S SUPPORTING CLAIM IS WRONG. All four arity-2 day ops in ops_ext.py — `day_wmean` (:107), `day_wstd` (:560), `day_signed_ratio` (:120), `day_topw_mean` (:575) — drop a minute entirely when the *other* argument is NaN; verified behaviourally (e.g. `day_wmean(a, b)` with b[9]=NaN equals `day_wmean(a[:9], b[:9])` exactly). The finding asserts the siblings' docstrings "explicitly say 'where both are finite'". That is true of `day_wmean` and `day_signed_ratio` only. `day_wstd`'s docstring is literally "Weighted population std over the day's minutes: sqrt(sum(|w| (x - m)^2) / sum(|w|))" — the same unqualified phrase "over the day's minutes", with the same joint-finite behaviour. So "the day's minutes" demonstrably means "the day's usable minutes" in this file, and `day_topw_mean` is not an outlier: two of four spell the qualifier out, two do not, and all four behave identically. What remains is a docstring omission shared with `day_wstd` — explicitly out of this review's scope (注释不报), and it changes no number.

3) IN PRODUCTION THE DIFFERENCE IS ZERO OR SUB-NOISE. I grepped every live use of this op (studies/F101..F115 */hypo3.yaml): `day_topw_mean(Ret, Amt)`, `(Close, Amt)`, `(Amt, Amt)`, `(in_index(Amt), Amt)`, `(Amt, in_index(Amt))`, `(in_slice(Ret,..), in_slice(Amt,..))`, `(nt_ts_autocorr_s1(Ret,3), Amt)`, `(pow_2(nt_ts_kurt(Close,30)), Amt)`. Six of the eight pass y and w with *identical* finiteness (same minute bar; and `in_index(x)` is NaN exactly where x is NaN, ops_ext.py:626) — there the two definitions agree to 1.1e-16, i.e. bit-identical in practice. Only the two `nt_ts_*` ones differ at all, and only via a deterministic warm-up prefix (`ts_*` along the minute axis NaNs the first d-1 minutes). There the median relative gap is 0.9% (rolling-std y) to 3.3% (F108's squared-kurtosis y), p99 5%-21%. The remaining realistic mask shape documented for this pipeline is Vwap missing on no-turnover minutes (AlphaCube docs/design.md:367) — y unreadable exactly where |w| is smallest: median gap 1.5%, and zero stock-days voided.

4) THE 24%-166% FIGURE IS A DENOMINATOR ARTIFACT. The harness uses `y ~ rng.normal(0,1)`, so the reference top-decile mean is a ~24-sample mean of a zero-mean variable: over 8000 reproduced stock-days its magnitude has median 0.186 and p05 0.017, while |kernel - fix| has median 0.037. Dividing one by the other manufactures arbitrarily large percentages. Both definitions are subsample means of the *same* readable y values, so the honest scale is the estimator's own standard error: |gap| / s.e. is median 0.14, p99 0.93 in the harness setting, and median ~0.31, p99 ~1.5 in the realistic warm-up setting. The two readings are statistically indistinguishable, not a 166% error. The harness also uses independent 20%/30% random minute NaN in y and w, a mask structure this pipeline does not produce: a dead/halted bar NaNs all fields together (store.py read_cube masks whole stock-days; synthetic.py NaNs every cube on non-trading days), and with one shared mask the two definitions agree exactly (median relative gap 0.000, p95 0.000 over 200 reps at M=241).

5) THE SUGGESTED FIX WOULD BE THE REGRESSION. (a) It makes the sample size random and missingness-driven: in the F108-shaped case the kernel averages a fixed 22 minutes per stock-day while the fix averages 9-22 (mean 16.4), where the count is a function of how much of the day's turnover fell inside the warm-up — i.e. it injects a turnover-concentration term into the estimator's noise. (b) It erases stock-days: with the day's turnover concentrated before the statistic exists (strictly decreasing Amt, y readable from minute 29), the kernel returns 0.5 and the fix returns NaN with 0 selected minutes. (c) It breaks the conditioning-set consistency the studies are built on: F115 h3 evaluates `sub(day_topw_mean(y,w), day_wmean(y,w))` — "top decile minus the all-minute weighted mean" — and `day_wmean` conditions on the joint-finite set, so under the fix the two legs would rank/average over different minute pools. (d) It would silently move the already-recorded ut/valid numbers of the h3_topw_* factors in F102 and F108.

Net: the complaint reduces to one missing clause in a docstring, shared with a sibling op, with no effect on any number or conclusion. Refuted.

result.corrected_fix: Do NOT apply the suggested code change. Changing the quantile pool to `isfinite(w)` only would (a) give the estimator a random, missingness-driven sample size (9-22 instead of a fixed 22 minutes in the F108-shaped case, where the count is itself a function of how much turnover fell in the warm-up), (b) return NaN and erase stock-days whose turnover is concentrated where y is unreadable (reproduced: kernel 0.5 vs fix NaN), (c) break the conditioning-set consistency of the designed contrast `sub(day_topw_mean(y,w), day_wmean(y,w))` used in F115 h3, since `day_wmean` ranks/averages over the joint-finite set, and (d) silently move the already-recorded ut/valid numbers of h3_topw_* in F102 and F108. The only defensible change is the reporter's own fallback — one clause in the prose, e.g. "Mean of y over the 10% of the day's minutes with the largest |w| (ties included), over the minutes where both are finite" — and `day_wstd`'s docstring (ops_ext.py:558-561) has the identical omission, so if it is touched at all both should be. That is a comment-only edit, outside this review's scope (注释不报), and changes no number.
